issue.body:
## Summary

Add a production-capable Google Vertex AI transport for Gemini to ADL's provider abstraction while reusing the existing Gemini semantic normalization. This is deferred provider work within v0.92.1 and is not a milestone-opening or GCP qualification dependency.

## Goal

Allow an ADL Runtime deployed in Google Cloud to invoke Gemini through Vertex AI using Google Cloud-native identity, regional configuration, governance, and observability.

## Required Outcome

ADL can select a distinct Vertex AI Gemini route that uses Application Default Credentials or workload identity, resolves an explicit project, location, and model identity, preserves governed UTS/ACC behavior, and produces reviewable provider evidence without changing the existing Gemini Developer API or Ollama baselines.

## Deliverables

- A Vertex AI provider transport integrated with the existing provider substrate and adapter boundary.
- Shared Gemini request, response, streaming, tool, safety, and error normalization reused across the Gemini Developer API and Vertex AI transports.
- ADC/workload-identity authentication with bounded token refresh and no embedded API keys.
- Explicit project, global-or-regional location, endpoint, publisher, and resolved model configuration.
- Provider receipts and telemetry that distinguish Gemini Developer API from Vertex AI and record redacted project, location, model identity, latency, usage, quota, and failure classification.
- Focused deterministic contract tests for endpoint construction, authentication boundaries, request/response mapping, streaming, UTS tool schemas and arguments, retries, cancellation, redaction, and error mapping.
- A separately authorized bounded live Vertex AI smoke-test plan; live paid execution is not implicit in this issue's creation.
- Configuration and operator documentation covering required IAM, `aiplatform.googleapis.com`, ADC, regional selection, quotas, and cleanup/non-claims.

## Acceptance Criteria

- ADL exposes Vertex AI as a distinct provider transport without duplicating the Gemini semantic codec.
- The transport authenticates through ADC or workload identity and does not require a stored Gemini API key.
- Requests resolve an explicit Google Cloud project, location, endpoint, publisher/model identity, timeout, and cancellation boundary.
- Streaming and non-streaming Gemini responses normalize into the existing ADL provider result contract.
- UTS tool declarations and returned tool calls preserve both tool names and arguments; tests reject incorrect argument mappings.
- IAM, authentication, quota, billing, safety, retryable/non-retryable errors, and redaction map into the common provider failure and observability contracts.
- Provider receipts distinguish `gemini_developer_api` from `vertex_ai` and contain no access tokens, credentials, prompt bodies, or raw sensitive responses.
- Existing Gemini Developer API, OpenRouter, Bedrock, and Ollama focused provider tests remain green.
- Any live Vertex call is separately authorized, cost-bounded, region-recorded, and reported as provider qualification rather than proof of the local Ollama portability baseline.

## Repo Inputs

- `adl/src/provider_adapter.rs`
- `adl/src/provider_substrate.rs`
- `adl/src/provider_communication.rs`
- `docs/validation/pvf_lanes.json`
- `.adl/docs/TBD/GCP_ACCOUNT_MOVE_IN_PLAN.md`
- `.adl/docs/TBD/ISSUE_268_GCP_SIX_RESIDENT_QUALIFICATION_PLAN.md`
- Issue #514, shared provider inference profiles
- Issue #509, GCP portability qualification

## Dependencies

- Coordinate with #514 so Vertex AI uses the shared provider-profile and capability model.
- The GCP project must have `aiplatform.googleapis.com` enabled before a live smoke test; the operator has confirmed it is enabled.
- Live validation requires explicit operator authorization, suitable IAM, quota, region/model availability, and a cost ceiling.
- This issue does not block milestone startup, #507, #509, or the local Ollama qualification lanes.

## Demo Expectations

- Deterministic fixture proof for both Gemini transports using the shared semantic codec.
- One optional, separately authorized live Vertex AI smoke test showing ADC identity, resolved model/location, governed tool calling, telemetry, and cost evidence.

## Non-goals

- Rewriting the existing Gemini adapter from scratch.
- Replacing Ollama, MLX, Bedrock, OpenRouter, or direct Gemini access.
- Making Vertex AI a milestone-opening, #268, #507, or #509 dependency.
- Broad GCP foundation, Terraform estate, organization-policy, networking, or production deployment work.
- Enabling APIs or mutating GCP IAM as part of issue creation.
- Rewriting the v0.92.1 planning package solely to insert this issue.
- Claiming all Gemini Developer API features are identical on Vertex AI without focused evidence.

## Issue-Graph Notes

- Treat as the next provider work item after PROV-A/PROV-B: `[v0.92.1][PROV-C]`.
- Schedule after milestone execution has started; it may proceed when provider capacity permits without delaying the opening wave.
- Keep the provider implementation and any broader GCP Terraform move-in work separately reviewable.

## Notes

The target architecture is one shared Gemini codec with separate transports: the existing Gemini Developer API route uses the Generative Language endpoint and Gemini credentials, while the Vertex AI route uses Vertex endpoints, Google Cloud project/location identity, and ADC/workload identity.

## Tooling Notes

- Use typed C-SDLC v2 lifecycle routes.
- Create and bootstrap only in this phase; do not bind a branch/worktree or start implementation.
- Use the focused provider validation lane and the smallest proving Rust tests before any broad validation.
- Any live provider call is a paid/external validation lane and must be explicitly authorized and truthfully recorded.
